stem: A 34-year-old woman reports distension of the hypochondrium and epigastrium for six months that worsens when she is frustrated at work. She sighs frequently, has breast distension and irritability before each period, an irregular cycle, and a sensation of a lump in the throat that comes and goes. The tongue is of normal color with a thin white coating. The pulse is wiry, most clearly on the left. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: When the Liver fails to ensure the smooth flow of Qi, Qi stagnates along the Liver channel, producing hypochondriac and epigastric distension, premenstrual breast distension and a fluctuating lump sensation in the throat. Sighing is the body's attempt to move stagnant Qi, and the link to frustration and irritability reflects the emotional component. An irregular cycle follows from disturbed Liver Qi. A normal-colored tongue and a wiry pulse confirm a stagnation pattern without Heat or deficiency.

distractorExplanations.B: Liver Blood deficiency presents with blurred vision, numbness, scanty pale menses, a pale tongue and a thin or choppy pulse; the distending, emotion-linked symptoms and normal tongue here point to stagnation, not deficiency.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Yang rising requires headache, dizziness and tinnitus from ascending Yang; none are present, and distension that comes and goes with mood is the hallmark of stagnation.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Fire blazing shows red face and eyes, bitter taste, thirst, a red tongue with a yellow coating and a rapid pulse; there are no Heat findings in this stem.

learningObjective: Identify Liver Qi stagnation from emotion-linked distension, sighing and a wiry pulse.

distinction.key: Distension that fluctuates with emotion, a normal-colored tongue and a wiry pulse indicate stagnation; Blood deficiency shows a pale tongue, a thin or choppy pulse and scanty menses.

stem: A 29-year-old woman reports blurred vision and floaters when reading for one year. She also has numbness and tingling of the limbs, muscle cramps at night, scanty pale menstrual flow, brittle nails, dry hair, and a dull-pale complexion. The tongue is pale, most noticeably on the sides, and slightly dry. The pulse is choppy. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: The Liver stores Blood, opens into the eyes, controls the sinews and manifests in the nails. When Liver Blood is deficient, the eyes are not nourished (blurred vision, floaters), the sinews are not moistened (numbness, tingling, cramps), the nails become brittle and menstrual flow becomes scanty and pale. The dull-pale complexion, pale tongue with paler sides and choppy pulse confirm Blood deficiency centered on the Liver.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Blood deficiency presents with palpitations, insomnia, poor memory and anxiety; the eye, sinew, nail and menstrual findings here locate the deficiency in the Liver.
distractorExplanations.B: Liver Yin deficiency adds Empty Heat or dryness with a red or uncoated tongue, night sweats and a thin rapid pulse; a pale tongue rules it out.
distractorExplanations.D: Spleen Qi deficiency would show poor appetite, loose stools, tiredness and an empty pulse; there are no digestive findings, and the Liver-specific signs are prominent.

learningObjective: Differentiate Liver Blood deficiency from Heart Blood deficiency using the Liver's sense organ, tissues and menstrual signs.

distinction.key: Eye, sinew, nail and menstrual signs locate Blood deficiency in the Liver; palpitations, insomnia and poor memory locate it in the Heart.

stem: A 52-year-old woman reports dry, gritty eyes and blurred vision for two years. She also has dizziness, numbness of the limbs, night sweats, a feeling of heat in the palms and soles in the evening, and very scanty menstrual flow. Her cheekbones become red in the afternoon. The tongue is red without coating. The pulse is thin (thready) and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Dry eyes, blurred vision, dizziness and numbness show that the Liver is failing to nourish its sense organ and sinews, as in Blood deficiency. The added night sweats, five-palm heat, afternoon malar flush, a red tongue without coating and a thin rapid pulse show that the deficiency has progressed to Yin, which can no longer cool and moisten, so Empty Heat arises. The discriminating finding is the red, uncoated tongue with a rapid pulse.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Blood deficiency shares the eye and sinew symptoms but has a pale tongue and a choppy or thin pulse without Empty Heat; the red uncoated tongue and night sweats rule it out.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Yang rising requires headache, irritability, tinnitus and a wiry pulse from ascending Yang; the picture here is of deficiency and Empty Heat without ascending signs.
distractorExplanations.D: Heart Yin deficiency causes palpitations, insomnia, anxiety and a redder tongue tip; the dominant eye and sinew symptoms locate the Yin deficiency in the Liver.

learningObjective: Differentiate Liver Yin deficiency from Liver Blood deficiency by the presence of Empty Heat and the tongue coating.

distinction.key: A red tongue without coating, a rapid pulse, night sweats and five-palm heat mark Liver Yin deficiency; Liver Blood deficiency has a pale tongue and no Empty Heat.

stem: A 58-year-old man reports recurrent throbbing headaches at the temples and behind the eyes for three years, worse with stress. He also has dizziness, tinnitus, irritability, dry eyes, and difficulty staying asleep. He has no thirst or bitter taste, and his bowel movements and urination are normal. The tongue is slightly red on the sides with a thin white coating. The pulse is wiry and thin (thready). Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Liver Yang ascending to the head causes throbbing temporal and retro-orbital headaches, dizziness and tinnitus, and disturbs the Ethereal Soul (Hun), causing irritability and poor sleep. Dry eyes and a thin component to the wiry pulse reflect the underlying Yin deficiency that allows Yang to rise. The discriminating findings are the absence of thirst, bitter taste, constipation and dark urine, together with a thin white coating, which show that ascending Yang, not Full Heat, is the mechanism.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Fire blazing would add thirst, bitter taste, red eyes, constipation, dark urine, a dry yellow coating and a full rapid pulse; these Full Heat signs are explicitly absent.
distractorExplanations.B: Liver Qi stagnation causes distension and mood fluctuation with a wiry pulse but not throbbing headache, dizziness and tinnitus from ascending Yang.
distractorExplanations.C: Heart Fire blazing produces palpitations, tongue ulcers, thirst, a redder tongue tip and a rapid pulse; the lateral headache and tinnitus point to the Liver, and Heat signs are absent.

learningObjective: Differentiate Liver Yang rising from Liver Fire blazing by the absence of Full Heat signs.

distinction.key: Liver Yang rising lacks the Full Heat signs of Liver Fire (thirst, bitter taste, constipation, dark urine, dry yellow coating, full rapid pulse) and often shows a thin component to the wiry pulse.

stem: A 41-year-old man reports a severe, throbbing headache at the temples for two weeks. His face and eyes are red and his eyes are painful. He has outbursts of anger, a bitter taste, thirst, dry stools, dark scanty urine, sudden-onset tinnitus, and two episodes of nosebleed. The tongue is red with redder sides and a dry yellow coating. The pulse is wiry, full (excess), and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.D: Damp-Heat in the Liver and Gallbladder

explanation: Full Heat in the Liver flares upward, causing a severe temporal headache, red face, red painful eyes (the Liver opens into the eyes), sudden tinnitus and outbursts of anger. Heat injures fluids, producing thirst, dry stools and dark urine, and forces Blood out of the vessels, causing nosebleed. The bitter taste, red tongue with redder sides, dry yellow coating and wiry, full, rapid pulse confirm Liver Fire.

distractorExplanations.B: Liver Yang rising produces headache and dizziness but lacks the Full Heat signs of thirst, constipation, dark urine, nosebleed, a dry yellow coating and a full rapid pulse.
distractorExplanations.C: Heart Fire blazing shows palpitations, tongue ulcers, insomnia and a redder tongue tip; the red eyes, temporal headache, redder tongue sides and wiry pulse locate the Fire in the Liver.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver and Gallbladder Damp-Heat would show a sticky yellow coating, a slippery pulse, nausea and heaviness; the coating here is dry and there are no Dampness findings.

learningObjective: Identify Liver Fire blazing and distinguish it from Heart Fire by location-specific findings.

distinction.key: Red painful eyes, temporal headache, bitter taste and redder tongue sides locate Fire in the Liver; tongue ulcers, palpitations and a redder tongue tip locate it in the Heart.

stem: A 6-year-old boy is brought in with a high fever that began two days ago. This morning he developed convulsions of the limbs, rigidity of the neck, clenched jaw, and upward-staring eyes, and he is now drowsy and difficult to rouse. The tongue is deep red (crimson) and stiff with a dry yellow coating. The pulse is wiry and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: In an acute febrile illness, extreme Heat burns the Yin and Blood that nourish the sinews and stirs internal Liver Wind, producing convulsions, neck rigidity, clenched jaw and upward-staring eyes. Heat entering the Pericardium clouds consciousness. The high fever, crimson stiff tongue and wiry rapid pulse confirm that the Wind arises from extreme Heat.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Yang rising generating Wind develops gradually in older adults with dizziness, tremor and numbness and without high fever; this is an acute febrile event in a child.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Blood deficiency generating Wind causes fine tremor and numbness with a pale tongue and thin or choppy pulse; the crimson tongue and high fever rule it out.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Fire blazing causes headache, red eyes, irritability and thirst but not convulsions; once Heat is extreme enough to stir Wind, the pattern is named by the Wind.

learningObjective: Identify Liver Wind arising from extreme Heat in an acute febrile presentation.

distinction.key: Acute high fever with a crimson tongue marks Wind from extreme Heat; Liver Yang rising generating Wind is chronic, afebrile and arises on a background of Yin deficiency.

stem: A 67-year-old man reports four months of severe dizziness with a tendency to lose his balance. He has developed a tremor of the hands, intermittent numbness of the fingers, throbbing headaches, tinnitus, and irritability. He has had no fever. The tongue is red, slightly deviated to one side, with a thin coating. The pulse is wiry and thin (thready). Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Throbbing headache, tinnitus, irritability and a wiry thin pulse indicate Liver Yang rising on a background of Yin deficiency. When ascending Yang becomes excessive it generates internal Wind, which manifests as movement: tremor, severe dizziness with loss of balance, numbness and a deviated tongue. These signs of Wind are the discriminating findings, and they warn of a possible Wind-stroke.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Yang rising alone explains the headache, tinnitus and irritability, but tremor, loss of balance, numbness and a deviated tongue show that Yang has progressed to generating Wind.
distractorExplanations.B: Liver Blood deficiency generating Wind shows fine tremor with a pale tongue, a choppy or thin pulse and no headache or irritability; the red tongue and ascending signs rule it out.
distractorExplanations.D: Extreme Heat generating Wind occurs in acute febrile illness with high fever, convulsions and a crimson tongue; this patient has no fever and a chronic course.

learningObjective: Recognize when Liver Yang rising has progressed to generating internal Wind.

distinction.key: Tremor, loss of balance, numbness and a deviated tongue are signs of Wind that mark progression beyond simple Liver Yang rising.

stem: A 71-year-old woman reports a fine tremor of the head and hands that has developed gradually over a year and worsens when she is tired. She also has tingling and numbness of the limbs, an occasional eyelid tic, blurred vision, mild dizziness, brittle nails, and a dull-pale complexion. She has no headache or irritability. The tongue is pale, thin, and slightly dry. The pulse is choppy. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Deficient Liver Blood fails to nourish the sinews and channels, and the resulting emptiness allows a mild internal Wind to arise, producing a fine tremor, tics, tingling and numbness that worsen with fatigue. Blurred vision, brittle nails, dull-pale complexion, a pale thin tongue and a choppy pulse confirm the underlying Liver Blood deficiency. The discriminating finding is the pale tongue with a choppy pulse and the absence of ascending-Yang signs.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Yang rising generating Wind shows coarser tremor with throbbing headache, irritability, a red tongue and a wiry pulse; the pale tongue and absence of headache rule it out.
distractorExplanations.B: Extreme Heat generating Wind is an acute febrile pattern with convulsions and a crimson tongue; this is a gradual, afebrile tremor.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Yin deficiency would show a red tongue without coating, night sweats and a rapid pulse; the pale tongue shows Blood rather than Yin deficiency, and it does not account for the tremor.

learningObjective: Differentiate Liver Blood deficiency generating Wind from Liver Yang rising generating Wind.

distinction.key: A fine tremor with a pale thin tongue and a choppy pulse, without headache or irritability, marks Wind from Blood deficiency; Yang-rising Wind shows a red tongue, a wiry pulse and ascending signs.

stem: A 35-year-old man reports three weeks of dragging pain in the lower abdomen that radiates to the testicles, with a sensation of the scrotum contracting. The pain began after several days of outdoor work in freezing rain, is aggravated in winter weather, and is relieved by a hot-water bottle. He has no lower back pain and normal urination. The tongue is pale with a moist white coating. The pulse is deep, wiry, and slow. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.A: Cold stagnating in the Liver channel
options.B: Damp-Heat in the Liver and Gallbladder

explanation: The Liver channel encircles the external genitalia and passes through the lower abdomen. External Cold invading the channel causes contraction and obstruction, producing dragging pain radiating to the testicles and scrotal contraction. Cold is relieved by warmth and aggravated by cold weather. The pale tongue with moist white coating and a deep, wiry, slow pulse confirm an Excess Cold pattern affecting the Liver channel; the acute onset after exposure and the wiry pulse distinguish it from deficiency Cold.

distractorExplanations.B: Liver and Gallbladder Damp-Heat would cause scrotal swelling, itching or heat with a red tongue, sticky yellow coating and slippery rapid pulse; all findings here are Cold.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Qi stagnation causes distension that fluctuates with emotion, not contracting pain that responds to temperature with a slow pulse and pale tongue.
distractorExplanations.D: Kidney Yang deficiency is chronic, with cold-aching lower back and knees, frequent pale urination and a deep weak pulse; this acute onset after exposure with a wiry pulse is Excess Cold.

learningObjective: Identify Cold stagnating in the Liver channel from genital pain with contraction relieved by warmth.

distinction.key: Acute contracting genital pain after cold exposure with a deep, wiry, slow pulse is Excess Cold in the Liver channel; Kidney Yang deficiency is chronic, with back weakness, urinary signs and a weak pulse.

stem: A 44-year-old man reports fullness and pain in the right hypochondrium for two months. He has a bitter taste, nausea, poor appetite with aversion to greasy food, a low-grade fever, scanty dark yellow urine, and itching and sweating of the scrotum. The tongue is red with a sticky (greasy) yellow coating, thicker on the sides. The pulse is wiry, slippery, and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.C: Damp-Heat in the Liver and Gallbladder

explanation: Damp-Heat obstructing the Liver and Gallbladder impairs the free flow of Qi and bile, causing hypochondriac fullness and pain, bitter taste, nausea and aversion to greasy food. Damp-Heat pouring down the Liver channel produces scrotal itching and sweating and dark scanty urine. The red tongue with a sticky yellow coating and a wiry, slippery, rapid pulse confirm combined Dampness (sticky coating, slippery) and Heat (red, yellow, rapid) in the Liver-Gallbladder.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Fire blazing shows a dry yellow coating, red eyes, headache and constipation without nausea or a slippery pulse; the sticky coating and scrotal sweating indicate Dampness.
distractorExplanations.B: Damp-Heat in the Spleen centers on epigastric fullness, heaviness and loose stools; the hypochondriac pain, bitter taste and genital findings follow the Liver-Gallbladder channels.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Qi stagnation causes distension with a wiry pulse and normal tongue; the red tongue, sticky yellow coating and slippery rapid pulse show Damp-Heat.

learningObjective: Differentiate Damp-Heat in the Liver and Gallbladder from Liver Fire blazing by the tongue coating and pulse.

distinction.key: A sticky yellow coating, slippery pulse, nausea and genital sweating indicate Damp-Heat; Liver Fire has a dry yellow coating, constipation and red eyes without Dampness.

stem: A 31-year-old woman has had premenstrual breast distension, frequent sighing, and moodiness for five years. Over the past three months she has also developed outbursts of anger, a feeling of heat in the face, mild thirst, and periods that come earlier and heavier than before. She has no headache, dizziness, or palpitations. The tongue is red on the sides with a thin coating. The pulse is wiry and slightly rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.B: Liver Qi stagnation transforming into Fire

explanation: Long-standing Liver Qi stagnation (breast distension, sighing, moodiness) generates Heat when stagnant Qi is compressed over time. The new Heat signs — anger outbursts, facial heat, thirst, early and heavy periods from Heat pushing Blood — together with red tongue sides and a slightly rapid wiry pulse show that the stagnation has transformed into Heat. The discriminating findings are the red sides and rapid pulse appearing on a history of stagnation.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Yang rising presents with headache, dizziness and tinnitus; these are explicitly absent and the picture is dominated by stagnation with emerging Heat.
distractorExplanations.C: Simple Liver Qi stagnation shows a normal-colored tongue and a wiry pulse without Heat; the red sides, faster pulse, facial heat and early heavy menses show transformation into Heat.
distractorExplanations.D: Heart Fire blazing causes palpitations, tongue ulcers, insomnia and a redder tongue tip; the Heat here is on the tongue sides and follows Liver stagnation.

learningObjective: Recognize the transformation of chronic Liver Qi stagnation into Fire.

distinction.key: Red tongue sides, a rapid wiry pulse, facial heat and early heavy menses added to a history of distension mark stagnation that has turned to Heat; simple stagnation has a normal tongue and no Heat.

stem: According to Zang Fu theory, impairment of which Liver function is the primary mechanism of Liver Qi stagnation?

options.D: ensuring the smooth flow of Qi

explanation: The Liver ensures the smooth, free flow of Qi throughout the body, which supports emotional ease, digestion and menstruation. When this function is impaired, typically by repressed emotions such as frustration or resentment, Qi stagnates, producing distension, sighing, moodiness and a wiry pulse.

distractorExplanations.A: Failure of the Liver to store Blood underlies Liver Blood deficiency and some bleeding or menstrual disorders, not the distension of Qi stagnation.
distractorExplanations.B: Impaired control of the sinews leads to cramps, stiffness, tremor or weakness, which belong to Blood deficiency or Wind patterns.
distractorExplanations.C: The Liver's opening into the eyes explains eye signs in Liver Blood deficiency or Liver Fire; it is not the mechanism of Qi stagnation.

learningObjective: Identify the Liver function whose impairment produces Liver Qi stagnation.

distinction.key: Qi stagnation reflects failure of the Liver's smooth-flow function; Blood deficiency reflects failure of its Blood-storing function.

stem: A 63-year-old woman reports palpitations for eight months that come on when she climbs stairs. She also has shortness of breath on exertion, tiredness, spontaneous daytime sweating, and a pale complexion. Her hands and feet are warm and she does not feel cold. She has no cough. The tongue is pale with a thin white coating. The pulse is empty (deficient). Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Heart Qi deficiency weakens the Heart's ability to propel Blood, so palpitations and shortness of breath appear or worsen on exertion, when the demand on Qi rises. Deficient Qi fails to hold sweat (spontaneous sweating) and to bring Blood to the face (pallor), and causes tiredness. The pale tongue and empty pulse confirm deficiency; the warm extremities and absence of feeling cold show that Yang is not yet involved.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Yang deficiency includes all signs of Heart Qi deficiency plus cold limbs, feeling cold, a bright-white face and a swollen wet tongue; the warm extremities rule it out.
distractorExplanations.B: Heart Blood deficiency presents with insomnia, poor memory, dizziness and a thin or choppy pulse; exertional palpitations, breathlessness and sweating point to Qi.
distractorExplanations.D: Lung Qi deficiency causes breathlessness and spontaneous sweating with weak voice, cough and frequent colds; palpitations on exertion locate the deficiency in the Heart.

learningObjective: Differentiate Heart Qi deficiency from Heart Yang deficiency by the presence or absence of Cold signs.

distinction.key: Heart Yang deficiency adds cold limbs, feeling cold and a swollen wet tongue to the exertional palpitations of Heart Qi deficiency.

stem: A 70-year-old man reports palpitations and shortness of breath on exertion for one year. He feels cold, his hands are cold, and he has a bright-white complexion, tiredness, and a sensation of stuffiness in the chest. He has no lower back pain, no swelling of the legs, and normal urination. The tongue is pale, swollen, and wet. The pulse is deep and weak. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Heart Yang deficiency fails to warm and propel Blood in the chest, causing palpitations, breathlessness on exertion and chest stuffiness. Deficient Yang fails to warm the body and limbs (feeling cold, cold hands) and produces a bright-white face. A pale, swollen, wet tongue and a deep weak pulse confirm Yang deficiency, and the cardiac and chest findings place it in the Heart.

distractorExplanations.B: Heart Qi deficiency shares palpitations and breathlessness but lacks Cold signs; the cold hands, feeling cold and wet swollen tongue show that Yang is deficient.
distractorExplanations.C: Kidney Yang deficiency is located by cold-aching lower back and knees, frequent pale urination and leg edema; these are absent, while palpitations and chest stuffiness point to the Heart.
distractorExplanations.D: Heart Blood stasis presents with stabbing chest pain, purple lips and tongue and a choppy or knotted pulse; the tongue here is pale and there is no stabbing pain.

learningObjective: Locate a Yang deficiency pattern in the Heart rather than the Kidney using organ-specific findings.

distinction.key: Palpitations and chest stuffiness locate Yang deficiency in the Heart; cold-aching back and knees, frequent pale urination and leg edema locate it in the Kidney.

stem: A 78-year-old man with years of palpitations and feeling cold is found by his family this morning very drowsy and barely responsive. He has profuse cold sweat on the forehead, ice-cold four limbs, cyanotic lips, and weak, shallow breathing. He has had no chest pain. The tongue is bluish-purple and short. The pulse is minute (faint) and barely perceptible. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: This is the extreme stage of Heart Yang deficiency. Yang can no longer hold fluids, so profuse cold sweat pours out despite the body being cold; it cannot warm the limbs (ice-cold extremities) or move Blood (cyanotic lips, bluish-purple short tongue), and the Spirit loses its residence, causing impaired consciousness. A minute, barely perceptible pulse confirms collapse. The apparently contradictory combination of profuse sweating in a cold patient is explained by Yang failing to consolidate the exterior.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Yang deficiency is chronic and stable, with a deep weak pulse and pale wet tongue; profuse cold sweat, impaired consciousness and a minute pulse indicate that Yang has collapsed.
distractorExplanations.B: Heart Blood stasis produces stabbing chest pain and a choppy or knotted pulse; despite the cyanosis, there is no chest pain, and the profuse sweat and minute pulse indicate collapse.
distractorExplanations.C: Phlegm misting the Heart clouds consciousness with a rattling throat, a swollen tongue with a sticky coating and a slippery pulse; there are no Phlegm findings here.

learningObjective: Recognize Heart Yang collapse as the extreme progression of Heart Yang deficiency.

distinction.key: Profuse cold sweat, ice-cold limbs, impaired consciousness and a minute pulse mark collapse; chronic Heart Yang deficiency has a deep weak pulse and no collapse signs.

stem: A 26-year-old female graduate student reports palpitations and difficulty falling asleep for six months. She also has dream-disturbed sleep, poor memory, anxiety, a tendency to be easily startled, dizziness, a dull-pale complexion, and pale lips. She has no night sweats and no feeling of heat. The tongue is pale, thin, and slightly dry. The pulse is choppy. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Heart Blood houses the Spirit (Shen); when it is deficient the Spirit has no residence, causing difficulty falling asleep, dream-disturbed sleep, anxiety, poor memory and being easily startled. Deficient Heart Blood also causes palpitations and fails to nourish the head and face (dizziness, dull-pale complexion, pale lips). A pale thin tongue and choppy pulse confirm Blood deficiency without Empty Heat.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Yin deficiency causes waking during the night, night sweats, malar flush and a red tongue without coating; this tongue is pale and Heat signs are absent.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Blood deficiency is located by blurred vision, numbness, cramps, brittle nails and scanty menses; the palpitations, startle and memory loss locate the deficiency in the Heart.
distractorExplanations.D: Heart Qi deficiency shows exertional palpitations, breathlessness, spontaneous sweating and an empty pulse; prominent insomnia and memory loss reflect deficient Blood failing to house the Spirit.

learningObjective: Differentiate Heart Blood deficiency from Heart Yin deficiency by tongue color and the absence of Empty Heat.

distinction.key: A pale tongue with difficulty falling asleep marks Heart Blood deficiency; a red uncoated tongue with night sweats and waking during the night marks Heart Yin deficiency.

stem: A 47-year-old man reports palpitations and waking frequently during the night for one year. He also has night sweats, mental restlessness, a feeling of heat in the evening, malar flush, dry mouth and throat, and poor memory. He has no mouth ulcers or bitter taste. The tongue is red without coating, with a redder tip and a deep midline crack reaching the tip. The pulse is thin (thready) and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Deficient Heart Yin fails to anchor the Spirit and cool the Heart, so Empty Heat agitates the Spirit, producing palpitations, waking during the night and mental restlessness. Empty Heat also causes night sweats, evening heat, malar flush and dry mouth and throat. The red, uncoated tongue with a redder tip and a Heart midline crack, plus a thin rapid pulse, confirm Yin deficiency with Empty Heat of the Heart.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Fire blazing is Full Heat with mouth ulcers, bitter taste, thirst, a yellow coating and a full rapid pulse; the absent coating and thin pulse indicate Empty Heat.
distractorExplanations.B: Heart Blood deficiency affects the Spirit similarly but with a pale tongue and no Heat signs; the red tongue, night sweats and malar flush show Yin deficiency.
distractorExplanations.D: Phlegm-Fire harassing the Heart shows manic agitation, a swollen tongue with a sticky yellow coating and a slippery rapid pulse; there are no Phlegm findings and the tongue is uncoated.

learningObjective: Differentiate Heart Yin deficiency (Empty Heat) from Heart Fire blazing (Full Heat).

distinction.key: A red tongue without coating and a thin rapid pulse with night sweats mark Empty Heat of Heart Yin deficiency; Heart Fire has a yellow coating, a full rapid pulse, ulcers and bitter taste.

stem: A 37-year-old man reports painful ulcers on the tongue for ten days. He also has palpitations, agitation, difficulty sleeping, thirst, a red face, and dark, scanty urine with burning on urination. The tongue is red with a redder, swollen tip and a yellow coating. The pulse is full (excess), rapid, and overflowing at the left distal position. Which mechanism best explains the burning, dark urination in this patient?

options.A: Heart Fire transmitted to the Small Intestine
options.B: Kidney Yin failing to cool the Lower Burner
options.D: Spleen Qi failing to transform fluids

explanation: The tongue ulcers, palpitations, agitation, insomnia, redder tongue tip and overflowing left distal pulse identify Heart Fire blazing. The Heart is interiorly-exteriorly paired with the Small Intestine, so Heart Fire can be transmitted to the Small Intestine and from there affect the Bladder, causing dark, scanty, burning urine. The urinary symptoms are therefore a branch of the Heart pattern.

distractorExplanations.B: Kidney Yin deficiency produces Empty Heat with a red uncoated tongue and thin rapid pulse; here the coating is yellow and the pulse full and overflowing, indicating Full Heat originating in the Heart.
distractorExplanations.C: Primary Bladder Damp-Heat shows a sticky yellow coating on the root and a slippery pulse, often with cloudy urine; the tongue ulcers, red tip and overflowing distal pulse point to the Heart as the source.
distractorExplanations.D: Spleen Qi failing to transform fluids produces Dampness, edema or loose stools with a pale tongue; it does not cause burning dark urine with Full Heat signs.

learningObjective: Explain urinary Heat signs in Heart Fire blazing through the Heart-Small Intestine relationship.

distinction.key: Burning urination accompanied by tongue ulcers, a redder tip and an overflowing distal pulse is Heart Fire transmitted via the Small Intestine; primary Bladder Damp-Heat has a sticky root coating and slippery pulse.

stem: A 55-year-old woman is brought in by her daughter, who reports that over several months she has become withdrawn and mentally confused. She mutters to herself, stares blankly at the wall for long periods, has a dull expression and lethargy, and has a rattling sound in the throat. She has no fever, thirst, or agitation. The tongue is swollen with a thick, sticky white coating. The pulse is slippery. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Phlegm obstructing the Heart's orifices clouds the Spirit, producing mental confusion, muttering, staring blankly, a dull expression and lethargy. The rattling throat, swollen tongue with a thick sticky white coating and slippery pulse confirm Phlegm. The quiet, withdrawn presentation with a white coating and no Heat signs distinguishes it from Phlegm-Fire.

distractorExplanations.A: Phlegm-Fire harassing the Heart causes manic agitation, shouting and insomnia with a red tongue, sticky yellow coating and slippery rapid pulse; this presentation is quiet and the coating white.
distractorExplanations.B: Heart Blood deficiency disturbs the Spirit with anxiety, insomnia and poor memory but with a pale thin tongue and choppy or thin pulse; it does not produce a sticky coating or clouded consciousness.
distractorExplanations.C: Spleen deficiency with Dampness causes heaviness and a muzzy head with tiredness and loose stools, but not clouding of the Spirit with muttering and blank staring.

learningObjective: Differentiate Phlegm misting the Heart from Phlegm-Fire harassing the Heart.

distinction.key: Quiet, withdrawn mental confusion with a sticky white coating and no Heat marks Phlegm misting the Heart; manic agitation with a sticky yellow coating and rapid pulse marks Phlegm-Fire.

stem: A 24-year-old man is brought in by his family after three weeks of insomnia, agitation, shouting at relatives, rapid incoherent speech, and inappropriate laughter. He also has palpitations, a bitter taste, and coughs up sticky sputum. The tongue is red and swollen with a sticky (greasy) yellow coating, red prickles on the tip, and a midline crack containing a yellow coating. The pulse is slippery, full (excess), and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Fire agitates the Spirit, causing insomnia, agitation, shouting, inappropriate laughter and palpitations, while Phlegm obstructs the Heart's orifices, causing incoherent speech. The sputum, swollen tongue with a sticky yellow coating, a crack containing a yellow coating and a slippery pulse confirm Phlegm; the red tongue with tip prickles and full rapid pulse confirm Fire. The discriminating findings are the sticky coating and slippery pulse, which add Phlegm to the Fire.

learningObjective: Differentiate Phlegm-Fire harassing the Heart from Heart Fire blazing by the signs of Phlegm.

distinction.key: A swollen tongue with a sticky yellow coating, sputum and a slippery pulse add Phlegm to the Fire; Heart Fire blazing alone lacks these Phlegm findings.

stem: A 66-year-old man reports attacks of stabbing chest pain for six months that radiate to the inner aspect of the left arm. He also has a feeling of oppression in the chest, palpitations, and purplish lips and nails. The pain is fixed in location and is not related to his mood. The tongue is purple, with distended, dark sublingual veins. The pulse is choppy. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Stagnant Blood in the Heart obstructs the vessels of the chest, producing fixed, stabbing chest pain radiating along the Heart channel to the inner left arm, chest oppression and palpitations. Blood stasis is confirmed by the purplish lips and nails, purple tongue, distended dark sublingual veins and choppy pulse. The fixed stabbing quality of the pain and the purple tongue are the discriminating findings.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Yang deficiency causes palpitations and chest stuffiness with feeling cold, a pale swollen wet tongue and a deep weak pulse; stabbing pain and a purple tongue indicate Blood stasis.
distractorExplanations.B: Heart Qi deficiency causes exertional palpitations, breathlessness and sweating with a pale tongue and empty pulse; it does not produce stabbing pain or a purple tongue.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Qi stagnation produces distending pain that moves and varies with emotion; this pain is fixed, stabbing and unrelated to mood.

learningObjective: Identify Heart Blood stasis from fixed stabbing chest pain with a purple tongue.

distinction.key: Fixed stabbing chest pain, a purple tongue and distended sublingual veins mark Heart Blood stasis; Heart Yang deficiency has a pale, swollen, wet tongue and Cold signs without stabbing pain.

stem: A 45-year-old man reports poor appetite and abdominal distension after eating for one year. He also has loose stools, tiredness, weakness of the limbs, and a sallow complexion. The distension does not vary with his mood. The tongue is pale with teeth marks on the sides and a thin white coating. The pulse is empty (deficient). Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Deficient Spleen Qi fails to transform and transport food, causing poor appetite, distension after eating and loose stools. Without adequate Food Qi the limbs and muscles are poorly nourished (tiredness, weak limbs) and the complexion becomes sallow. A pale tongue with teeth marks and an empty pulse confirm Spleen Qi deficiency.

distractorExplanations.A: Spleen Yang deficiency adds cold limbs, feeling cold and a pale wet tongue with a deep slow pulse; no Cold signs are present.
distractorExplanations.B: Cold-Damp invading the Spleen is an acute Excess pattern with heaviness, a thick sticky white coating and a slippery pulse; this is a chronic deficiency with a thin coating and empty pulse.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Qi stagnation causes distension that varies with emotion and a wiry pulse; this distension follows eating, is unrelated to mood and comes with an empty pulse.

learningObjective: Identify Spleen Qi deficiency and distinguish its distension from that of Liver Qi stagnation.

distinction.key: Distension after eating with tiredness, a pale teeth-marked tongue and an empty pulse marks Spleen Qi deficiency; emotion-linked distension with a wiry pulse marks Liver Qi stagnation.

stem: A 57-year-old woman reports loose stools containing undigested food for three years. She also has a dull abdominal ache that is relieved by warmth and by pressure, cold limbs, a constant feeling of cold, tiredness, and poor appetite. She has no lower back pain and the stools are not worse in the early morning. The tongue is pale, swollen, and wet with a thin white coating. The pulse is deep, weak, and slow. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Spleen Yang deficiency fails to warm and transform food, so stools are loose and contain undigested food, and the abdomen aches dully. Pain relieved by pressure and warmth, a chronic course and a weak pulse show deficiency Cold rather than Excess Cold. Cold limbs, feeling cold, a pale swollen wet tongue and a deep slow pulse confirm Yang deficiency, and the digestive focus without back or early-morning symptoms locates it in the Spleen.

distractorExplanations.B: Cold-Damp invading the Spleen is acute and Excess, with fullness aggravated by pressure, heaviness, a thick sticky white coating and a slippery pulse; this chronic ache relieved by pressure with a weak pulse is deficiency.
distractorExplanations.C: Spleen Qi deficiency shares the digestive signs but lacks cold limbs, feeling cold and a wet tongue with a slow pulse.
distractorExplanations.D: Kidney Yang deficiency produces early-morning diarrhea with cold-aching lower back and knees and frequent pale urination; these Kidney findings are absent.

learningObjective: Differentiate Spleen Yang deficiency (Empty Cold) from Cold-Damp invading the Spleen (Full Cold).

distinction.key: A chronic ache relieved by pressure with a weak pulse and thin coating is Spleen Yang deficiency; acute fullness worse with pressure, a thick sticky white coating and a slippery pulse is Cold-Damp invasion.

stem: A 62-year-old woman reports a bearing-down sensation in the lower abdomen for two years, worse when standing for long periods or when tired. She has a sensation of something descending in the vagina, frequent urge to urinate, chronic loose stools, tiredness, and poor appetite. She has no bruising or abnormal bleeding and does not feel cold. The tongue is pale with a thin white coating. The pulse is weak. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Spleen Qi has a rising function that holds the organs in place. When chronic Spleen Qi deficiency progresses, this raising function fails and Qi sinks, causing a bearing-down sensation, vaginal prolapse sensation, frequent urination and chronic loose stools, all worse with standing or fatigue. Poor appetite, tiredness, a pale tongue and a weak pulse confirm the underlying deficiency. The bearing-down sensation and prolapse are the discriminating findings.

distractorExplanations.A: Spleen Qi deficiency explains the tiredness, poor appetite and loose stools, but the bearing-down sensation and prolapse show that the raising function has failed, which is the more specific diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.C: Spleen not controlling Blood is defined by bleeding (bruising, menorrhagia, blood in stools); no bleeding is reported.
distractorExplanations.D: Spleen Yang deficiency adds cold limbs, feeling cold and a wet tongue; the patient does not feel cold and the dominant feature is sinking.

learningObjective: Identify Spleen Qi sinking from bearing-down sensations and prolapse on a background of Spleen Qi deficiency.

distinction.key: A bearing-down sensation and prolapse show failure of the Spleen's raising function, which distinguishes Spleen Qi sinking from simple Spleen Qi deficiency.

stem: A 38-year-old woman reports easy bruising for eight months. She also has small purple spots on the legs, heavy periods with pale, watery blood, tiredness, poor appetite, loose stools, and a sallow complexion. The tongue is pale. The pulse is thin (thready) and weak. Which mechanism best explains her bleeding?

options.A: Heat in the Blood forcing it out of the vessels
options.C: Spleen Qi failing to hold Blood in the vessels
options.D: Empty Heat from Yin deficiency injuring the vessels

explanation: The Spleen controls Blood by holding it within the vessels. When Spleen Qi is deficient, as shown by tiredness, poor appetite, loose stools and a sallow complexion, Blood leaks out, causing easy bruising, purpura and heavy menses. Pale, watery menstrual blood, a pale tongue and a thin weak pulse confirm a deficiency-type bleeding without Heat or stasis.

distractorExplanations.A: Blood Heat causes bleeding with bright or dark red blood, a red tongue and a rapid pulse; the pale blood, pale tongue and weak pulse rule it out.
distractorExplanations.B: Blood stasis causes bleeding with dark clots, fixed stabbing pain, a purple tongue and a choppy pulse; none are present.
distractorExplanations.D: Empty Heat bleeding comes with night sweats, malar flush, a red uncoated tongue and a thin rapid pulse; there are no Heat signs here.

learningObjective: Explain how Spleen Qi deficiency produces bleeding and distinguish it from Heat-type bleeding.

distinction.key: Pale watery blood with a pale tongue, weak pulse and digestive deficiency marks Spleen not controlling Blood; Blood Heat shows bright red blood, a red tongue and a rapid pulse.

stem: A 30-year-old man reports epigastric and abdominal fullness for four days, beginning after a week of camping in steady rain during which he ate mostly cold, uncooked food. He also has a heavy sensation in the head and body, poor appetite, nausea, loose stools, a sweetish sticky taste in the mouth, and no thirst. The tongue has a thick, sticky white coating. The pulse is slippery and slow. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Exposure to damp weather and cold, raw food allows Cold-Damp to invade and obstruct the Spleen, impairing transformation and transportation. This causes epigastric fullness, poor appetite, nausea, loose stools and a sweetish sticky taste. Dampness weighs down the head and body, and the absence of thirst, thick sticky white coating and slippery slow pulse confirm Cold-Damp. The acute onset after exposure marks it as an Excess pattern.

distractorExplanations.B: Damp-Heat in the Spleen shows thirst without desire to drink, a red tongue, a sticky yellow coating and a slippery rapid pulse; the white coating, absence of thirst and slow pulse indicate Cold.
distractorExplanations.C: Spleen Qi deficiency is chronic, with tiredness, a thin coating and an empty pulse; the thick coating, heaviness and acute onset indicate a pathogenic invasion.

learningObjective: Differentiate Cold-Damp invading the Spleen from Damp-Heat in the Spleen.

distinction.key: A thick sticky white coating, absence of thirst and a slippery slow pulse mark Cold-Damp; a sticky yellow coating, thirst without desire to drink and a slippery rapid pulse mark Damp-Heat.

stem: A 39-year-old woman reports epigastric and abdominal fullness for ten days. She also has nausea, loose foul-smelling stools, thirst without a desire to drink, a heavy sensation in the body, a low-grade fever, and scanty dark urine. She has no hypochondriac pain, no bitter taste, and no genital itching or discharge. The tongue is red with a sticky (greasy) yellow coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. explanation: Damp-Heat obstructing the Spleen impairs transformation, producing epigastric and abdominal fullness, nausea and loose foul-smelling stools. stem: A 50-year-old man reports fatigue and poor appetite for five years. He also has loose stools, a persistent feeling of heaviness in the limbs, a muzzy (fuzzy) head, and mild abdominal fullness after meals. He does not feel cold and has no thirst. The tongue is pale and swollen with teeth marks and a sticky (greasy) white coating. The pulse is soggy (soft). Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Long-standing Spleen deficiency (fatigue, poor appetite, loose stools, pale teeth-marked tongue) has led to failure of fluid transformation, so Dampness accumulates as a secondary pathogen. Dampness produces heaviness of the limbs, a muzzy head, post-prandial fullness, a swollen tongue with a sticky white coating and a soggy pulse. This is a combined deficiency (root) and excess (branch) pattern; the sticky coating and soggy pulse are the discriminating findings.

distractorExplanations.D: Spleen Yang deficiency would add cold limbs, feeling cold and a deep slow weak pulse; the patient does not feel cold.

learningObjective: Recognize the combined pattern of Spleen deficiency with Dampness as root deficiency with a branch excess.

distinction.key: A sticky coating, heaviness, a muzzy head and a soggy pulse added to chronic Spleen Qi deficiency signs mark accumulated Dampness; simple Spleen Qi deficiency has a thin coating and an empty pulse.

stem: In Spleen deficiency, failure of which Spleen function leads most directly to the formation of internal Dampness?
explanation: The Spleen transforms and transports both food and fluids. When this function fails, fluids are not separated and moved, so they accumulate as internal Dampness, which can further congeal into Phlegm. This is why chronic Spleen deficiency so often presents with heaviness, a sticky coating and loose stools.

stem: A 58-year-old man reports a weak, chronic cough for two years. He becomes slightly short of breath on exertion, has a weak voice and no desire to talk, sweats spontaneously during the day, and catches colds easily. His sputum is scant and watery. The tongue is pale with a thin white coating. The pulse is empty, most noticeably at the right front (Cun) position. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: The Lung governs Qi and respiration and spreads the Wei Qi that keeps the pores closed. When Lung Qi is deficient, the cough is weak and chronic, breathing becomes short on exertion because exertion consumes Qi, and the voice is weak. Deficient Wei Qi lets sweat leak out by day and leaves the patient open to repeated colds. A pale tongue and an empty pulse at the right front (Lung) position confirm Qi deficiency of the Lung. The discriminating finding is spontaneous daytime sweating with a pale tongue, rather than night sweats with a red, peeled tongue.

distractorExplanations.D: Phlegm-Damp produces profuse sticky white sputum, chest oppression, a thick sticky coating and a slippery pulse; the sputum here is scant and the coating thin.

learningObjective: Identify Lung Qi deficiency from a chronic weak cough with spontaneous daytime sweating and an empty right front pulse.

distinction.key: Spontaneous daytime sweating with a pale tongue indicates Lung Qi deficiency; night sweats with a red, peeled tongue indicate Lung Yin deficiency.

stem: A 44-year-old woman reports a dry cough for eight months, with scanty, sticky sputum that is occasionally streaked with blood. Her throat is dry and tickly, worse in the evening, and her voice has become hoarse. She has night sweats, a malar flush in the afternoon, and a feeling of heat in the palms and soles. The tongue is red and dry, with no coating. The pulse is thin (thready) and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Lung Yin deficiency deprives the Lung of moisture, giving a chronic dry cough with scanty sticky sputum, a dry tickly throat and a hoarse voice. Deficient Yin generates Empty Heat, seen as night sweats, an afternoon malar flush, five-palm heat and blood-streaked sputum. The discriminating findings are the eight-month course with Empty Heat signs and a coatless tongue, which separate an internal Yin deficiency from an exterior Dryness invasion.

distractorExplanations.B: Phlegm-Heat produces profuse sticky yellow sputum, a thick sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse; here the sputum is scanty and the tongue has no coating.
distractorExplanations.D: Lung Qi deficiency shows a weak cough, spontaneous daytime sweating, a pale tongue and an empty pulse, with no dryness or Heat signs.

learningObjective: Differentiate Lung Yin deficiency from Dryness injuring the Lung using chronicity, Empty Heat signs and the tongue coating.

stem: A 27-year-old woman reports a fever with slight aversion to cold that began two days ago. She has a sore, red, swollen throat, a cough with scanty yellow sputum, slight thirst, mild sweating and a headache. The tongue is slightly red on the tip and sides with a thin white coating. The pulse is floating and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Wind-Heat invades the Lung's defensive (exterior) layer, so fever predominates over a slight aversion to cold. Heat rising to the throat makes it sore, red and swollen; Heat mildly injures fluids, giving thirst and scanty yellow sputum, and opens the pores, giving mild sweating. A slightly red tip and sides with a thin coating show Heat still at the exterior, and the floating, rapid pulse confirms an exterior Heat pattern. The discriminating findings are the floating, rapid pulse with a sore, red throat.

distractorExplanations.A: Wind-Cold has marked aversion to cold with mild fever, no sweating, no thirst and a floating-tight pulse; a learner who fixes on the words 'aversion to cold' without weighing fever, throat and pulse would choose it.
distractorExplanations.B: Phlegm-Heat in the Lung is interior: no aversion to cold, profuse sticky yellow sputum, a thick sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse. The floating pulse and two-day exterior onset rule it out.
distractorExplanations.C: Lung Yin deficiency is chronic, with night sweats, a red tongue without coating and a thin-rapid pulse; it does not cause an acute fever with aversion to cold.

distinction.key: Fever predominating, a sore red throat, thirst and a floating-rapid pulse mark Wind-Heat; marked chills, no sweating and a floating-tight pulse mark Wind-Cold.

stem: A 63-year-old man who is overweight reports a chronic cough for three years. He brings up profuse white, sticky sputum that is easy to expectorate, mostly in the morning. He feels oppression in the chest, becomes short of breath when lying flat, and has occasional nausea and a poor appetite. The tongue is swollen with a thick, sticky white coating. The pulse is slippery. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Phlegm-Damp, usually generated by a weak Spleen and stored in the Lung, obstructs the descent of Lung Qi, producing a chronic cough with profuse white sticky sputum that comes up easily, chest oppression and breathlessness when lying down. Nausea and poor appetite reflect the Spleen-Stomach origin of the Dampness. The swollen tongue with a thick sticky white coating and the slippery pulse confirm Phlegm without Heat. The discriminating finding is white sputum with a white sticky coating rather than yellow sputum with a yellow coating.

distinction.key: White sputum with a thick sticky white coating and a slippery pulse indicate Phlegm-Damp; yellow sputum, a red tongue with a sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse indicate Phlegm-Heat.

stem: A 51-year-old woman reports a loud, barking cough for ten days. It began after a cold, but she no longer has chills. She now coughs up profuse, thick, yellow-green sputum and has oppression in the chest, wheezing, a sensation of heat, thirst and restless sleep. The tongue is red and swollen with a thick, sticky yellow coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Phlegm-Heat in the Lung is an interior Excess pattern: Heat condenses fluids into thick yellow-green Phlegm, which obstructs the descent of Lung Qi and causes a barking cough, chest oppression and wheezing. Heat produces a sensation of heat, thirst and restless sleep. A red, swollen tongue with a thick sticky yellow coating and a slippery, rapid pulse confirm Phlegm with Heat. The discriminating findings are the absence of chills and a slippery rather than floating pulse, showing that the pathogen has moved from the exterior to the interior.

learningObjective: Differentiate interior Phlegm-Heat in the Lung from exterior Wind-Heat after an initial cold.

distinction.key: Absence of chills, a thick sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse mark interior Phlegm-Heat; aversion to cold, a thin coating and a floating-rapid pulse mark exterior Wind-Heat.

stem: A 35-year-old man reports a dry cough for one week that began during a dry, windy autumn spell. He has scanty, sticky sputum that is hard to expectorate, a dry nose, dry lips, a dry throat, dry skin and slight thirst. He has no fever, night sweats or afternoon heat. The tongue is of normal color with a thin, dry coating. The pulse is slightly floating. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Dryness, the climatic factor of autumn, injures the Lung's fluids first, giving a dry cough with scanty, sticky sputum and dryness of the Lung's opening and tissues: nose, throat, lips and skin. The recent onset in dry weather, the slightly floating pulse and a tongue of normal color with a thin but dry coating show an external Dryness that has not yet consumed Yin. The discriminating finding is dryness of the orifices with a thin dry coating and no Empty Heat signs.

distractorExplanations.A: Lung Yin deficiency also produces a dry cough, but it is chronic, with night sweats, an afternoon malar flush and a red tongue without coating; the learner who equates dryness with Yin deficiency ignores the one-week course and the intact coating.
distractorExplanations.B: Wind-Heat presents with fever, a sore red throat, mild sweating, a red tongue tip and a floating-rapid pulse; dryness of the nose, lips and skin without fever points to Dryness.
distractorExplanations.D: Phlegm-Heat has profuse yellow sputum, a thick sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse; here the sputum is scanty and the coating thin and dry.

learningObjective: Identify Dryness injuring the Lung from a recent dry cough with dryness of the orifices in dry weather.

distinction.key: A recent onset in dry weather with dry orifices and a thin dry coating marks Dryness; a chronic course with Empty Heat and a coatless red tongue marks Lung Yin deficiency.

stem: A patient has had a cough with thin, white sputum for one day, with marked aversion to cold, a slight fever, no sweating, a stuffy nose and aching in the body. Which pulse quality is most consistent with this presentation?
explanation: This is Wind-Cold invading the Lung with Cold predominating. A floating pulse reflects the Upright Qi rising to meet a pathogen at the exterior, and a tight pulse reflects Cold contracting the channels and pores, which also explains the absence of sweating and the body aches. The floating, tight pulse is the classic pulse of exterior Wind-Cold.

distractorExplanations.A: Floating-rapid is the pulse of exterior Wind-Heat, which has fever predominating, a sore throat and thirst; it fits a learner who notices the fever but not the marked chills.

distractorExplanations.D: A soggy pulse indicates Dampness or deficiency; it is soft and lacks the tension that Cold produces.

learningObjective: Identify the pulse quality characteristic of Wind-Cold invading the Lung.

distinction.key: Tightness added to a floating pulse reflects Cold contracting the exterior; rapidity added to a floating pulse reflects exterior Heat.

stem: A 57-year-old man reports a chronic, dull lower backache with a feeling of cold in the back for four years. His knees and feet are always cold, he passes abundant clear urine and gets up twice at night to urinate, and he has low libido with impotence. He is tired and apathetic, with a bright-white complexion. The tongue is pale, swollen and wet. The pulse is deep, weak and slow. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Kidney Yang is the source of warmth for the whole body and the fire of the Gate of Vitality (Ming Men). When it is deficient, the lower back and knees ache and feel cold, the feet are cold and sexual function declines. The Bladder receives too little Yang to transform fluids, so urine is abundant and clear, with nocturia. Fatigue, apathy and a bright-white complexion reflect deficient Yang, and a pale, swollen, wet tongue with a deep, weak, slow pulse confirms interior Empty Cold. The discriminating findings are the Cold signs with abundant clear urine.

distractorExplanations.A: Kidney Yin deficiency shares the backache but presents with night sweats, a dry mouth at night, scanty dark urine, a red tongue without coating and a thin-rapid pulse, the Heat counterpart of this picture.
distractorExplanations.B: Kidney Essence deficiency is defined by developmental or premature-aging signs such as poor bone development, loose teeth and early greying, without marked Cold; the prominent Cold signs, wet tongue and slow pulse here point to Yang.
distractorExplanations.C: Kidney failing to receive Qi requires breathlessness with difficult inhalation; there are no respiratory findings.

learningObjective: Identify Kidney Yang deficiency from lower back Cold, abundant clear urine and a deep, weak, slow pulse.

distinction.key: Cold back and limbs, abundant clear urine, a pale wet tongue and a slow pulse mark Kidney Yang deficiency; night sweats, scanty dark urine and a red coatless tongue mark Kidney Yin deficiency.

stem: A 62-year-old woman reports a gradually worsening, low-pitched tinnitus for one year. She has dizziness, a sore and weak lower back and knees, poor memory, a dry mouth and throat at night, night sweats, constipation with dry stools and scanty dark urine. The tongue is red with no coating. The pulse is floating-empty and slightly rapid, weakest at both rear (Chi) positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: The Kidney opens into the ears, nourishes the brain (Sea of Marrow) and governs the lower back and knees. Kidney Yin deficiency fails to nourish the ears and brain, producing a gradual, low-pitched tinnitus, dizziness and poor memory. Deficient Yin fails to moisten, causing a dry mouth at night, dry stools and scanty dark urine, and the resulting Empty Heat produces night sweats. The red, coatless tongue and a floating-empty, rapid pulse weakest at the rear positions confirm Kidney Yin deficiency. The discriminating finding is the gradual, low-pitched tinnitus with an empty pulse rather than a sudden, loud tinnitus with a wiry pulse.

distractorExplanations.B: Liver Yang rising causes a sudden, loud, high-pitched tinnitus with headache, irritability and a wiry pulse; the learner who links all tinnitus to ascending Yang overlooks the gradual onset, low pitch and empty pulse.
distractorExplanations.C: Kidney Yang deficiency shares the backache and weak knees but gives cold limbs, abundant clear urine, a pale wet tongue and a deep, slow pulse, the opposite of the dryness and Heat here.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Blood deficiency causes dizziness and poor memory with a pale tongue and a thin or choppy pulse; night sweats, a red coatless tongue and the back and knee signs point to Kidney Yin.

learningObjective: Differentiate Kidney Yin deficiency from Liver Yang rising in a patient with tinnitus and dizziness.

distinction.key: Gradual, low-pitched tinnitus with an empty pulse weak at the rear positions marks Kidney Yin deficiency; sudden, loud tinnitus with headache and a wiry pulse marks Liver Yang rising.

stem: A 3-year-old boy is brought in because he was late to sit, stand and walk and still speaks only a few words. His fontanelle closed late, his bones are soft and his teeth came in slowly. He is small for his age and his hair is sparse, but his appetite and stools are normal and his limbs are not cold. The tongue is pale with a thin white coating. The pulse is thin (thready) and weak. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Kidney Essence (Jing), inherited from the parents, governs growth and development, the bones, the marrow and brain, the teeth and the hair. Insufficient prenatal Essence in a child produces the classic developmental delays: late sitting, standing, walking and speech, late closure of the fontanelle, soft bones, slow tooth eruption, short stature and sparse hair. The pale tongue and thin, weak pulse show deficiency without marked Heat or Cold. The discriminating finding is delayed development of bones, teeth and brain with no digestive or Cold signs.

distractorExplanations.A: Spleen Qi deficiency in a child shows poor appetite, loose stools, tiredness and thin muscles; this child's appetite and stools are normal, and Spleen deficiency does not explain late fontanelle closure or delayed teeth.
distractorExplanations.B: Kidney Yang deficiency would add cold limbs, a pale wet tongue and a deep, slow pulse; this child has no Cold signs, so the deficiency is of Essence rather than of Kidney Yang.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Blood deficiency causes dizziness, blurred vision, dry hair and nails and pale lips; it does not account for delayed bone, tooth and speech development.

learningObjective: Identify Kidney Essence deficiency as the pattern underlying developmental delay in a young child.

distinction.key: Delayed growth of bones, teeth, fontanelle and speech with normal digestion marks Kidney Essence deficiency; poor appetite and loose stools mark Spleen Qi deficiency.

stem: A 76-year-old woman reports urinary dribbling after voiding and occasional incontinence for two years. She urinates frequently, with pale urine and a weak stream, has a chronic thin, white vaginal discharge, and her lower back feels sore and weak. Her breathing is normal and she has no burning on urination. The tongue is pale. The pulse is deep and weak, especially at both rear (Chi) positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Kidney Qi holds the lower orifices closed. When it is not firm, fluids leak downward: dribbling after urination, incontinence, frequent pale urine with a weak stream and a chronic thin, white vaginal discharge. The sore, weak lower back, pale tongue and deep, weak pulse at both rear positions locate the deficiency in the Kidney. The discriminating feature is a failure of holding at the lower orifices without breathlessness or Heat.

distractorExplanations.A: Kidney failing to receive Qi is a failure of the Kidney to grasp Lung Qi, with shortness of breath and difficult inhalation; this patient's breathing is normal.
distractorExplanations.C: Bladder Damp-Heat produces burning, urgent urination with dark or cloudy urine, a sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse; the learner who links any urinary frequency with Damp-Heat misses the pale urine and weak pulse.
distractorExplanations.D: Kidney Yin deficiency gives scanty dark urine, night sweats and a red coatless tongue; pale urine and a pale tongue point to deficient Kidney Qi rather than Yin.

learningObjective: Explain how Kidney Qi not firm produces leakage from the lower orifices.

distinction.key: Both are Kidney Qi failures; leakage from the lower orifices with normal breathing marks Kidney Qi not firm, while difficult inhalation marks Kidney failing to receive Qi.

stem: A 71-year-old man reports shortness of breath for six years that is worse on exertion. He finds it harder to breathe in than to breathe out, and he leaks urine when he coughs. He also has a sore lower back, cold limbs, spontaneous sweating and frequent clear urination. He has no edema and little sputum. The tongue is pale. The pulse is deep and weak, especially at both rear (Chi) positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.C: Kidney Yang deficiency with water overflowing

explanation: The Lung governs exhalation and the Kidney grasps and holds down inhaled Qi. When Kidney Qi or Yang is too weak to receive Qi, breathlessness is chronic and worse on exertion, and inhalation is more difficult than exhalation. Urine leaking with coughing, a sore lower back, cold limbs, frequent clear urine and a deep, weak pulse at both rear positions show Kidney involvement, while spontaneous sweating reflects the accompanying Lung Qi weakness. The discriminating finding is difficult inhalation together with Kidney signs and weak rear pulses.

distractorExplanations.A: Lung Qi deficiency causes shortness of breath, a weak voice and spontaneous sweating with a weak right front pulse, but it does not explain difficult inhalation, urinary leakage with coughing, low backache or weak rear pulses; the learner who stops at the respiratory complaint picks it.
distractorExplanations.B: Phlegm-Damp produces profuse white sputum, chest oppression, a thick sticky coating and a slippery pulse; this patient has little sputum and a weak pulse.
distractorExplanations.C: Kidney Yang deficiency with water overflowing shows edema and scanty urine with a swollen, wet tongue; this patient has no edema and his urine is frequent and clear.

learningObjective: Differentiate Kidney failing to receive Qi from Lung Qi deficiency in chronic breathlessness.

distinction.key: Difficult inhalation with low backache, urine leaking on coughing and weak rear pulses marks Kidney failing to receive Qi; Lung Qi deficiency lacks the Kidney signs.

stem: A 39-year-old man reports scanty dark urine with occasional blood for two months, without burning pain or urgency. He has a malar flush in the afternoon, heat in the palms and soles, night sweats, nocturnal emissions with dreams, a sore lower back and mental restlessness. The tongue is red, cracked and without coating. The pulse is floating-empty and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.A: Kidney Yin deficiency with Empty Fire
options.C: Full Heat in the Small Intestine

explanation: Long-standing Kidney Yin deficiency gives rise to Empty Fire, which flares and stirs the Blood, causing scanty dark urine with blood, and harasses the Mind and the Essence, causing restlessness and nocturnal emissions with dreams. An afternoon malar flush, five-palm heat and night sweats are classic Empty Heat signs, and the sore lower back locates the root in the Kidney. A red, cracked tongue without coating and a floating-empty, rapid pulse confirm Yin deficiency with Empty Heat. The discriminating findings are blood in the urine without burning or urgency, together with a coatless tongue and an empty pulse.

distractorExplanations.B: Bladder Damp-Heat also produces dark urine and sometimes blood, but with burning, urgency and frequency, a sticky yellow coating on the root and a slippery-rapid pulse; it is a Full pattern, whereas this tongue has no coating and the pulse is empty.
distractorExplanations.C: Full Heat in the Small Intestine follows Heart Fire and shows burning urination with mouth and tongue ulcers, thirst, a red tip with a yellow coating and an overflowing-rapid pulse; it is Full Heat, not Empty Heat.
distractorExplanations.D: Kidney Qi not firm causes nocturnal emissions without dreams, pale frequent urine and dribbling with a pale tongue; dreams, Heat signs and a red tongue point to Yin deficiency with Empty Fire.

learningObjective: Differentiate Kidney Yin deficiency with Empty Fire from Full Heat patterns of the Lower Burner in a patient with blood in the urine.

distinction.key: Blood in the urine without burning or urgency, with a coatless red tongue and a floating-empty pulse, marks Empty Fire; burning urgency with a sticky yellow root coating and a slippery pulse marks Bladder Damp-Heat.

stem: A 69-year-old woman reports pitting edema of the ankles and lower legs for five months. She passes only small amounts of pale urine, her lower back and knees feel cold and sore, and her limbs are cold. She has palpitations and breathlessness on exertion, and when she lies flat she coughs up thin, watery sputum. The tongue is pale, swollen and wet, with a white coating. The pulse is deep, weak and slow. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.C: Kidney Yang deficiency with water overflowing

explanation: Kidney Yang transforms fluids and governs their excretion through the Bladder. When it is so deficient that fluids accumulate, water overflows into the tissues of the lower body as pitting edema, and urine becomes scanty because fluids are neither transformed nor excreted. Water rising to insult the Heart and Lung causes palpitations and breathlessness. A cold back, knees and limbs, a pale, swollen, wet tongue and a deep, weak, slow pulse confirm the Kidney Yang root. The discriminating finding is scanty urine with leg edema and palpitations, which marks the progression from simple Kidney Yang deficiency to water overflowing.

distractorExplanations.A: Heart Yang deficiency produces palpitations, cold limbs and a deep weak pulse, but not scanty urine, pitting edema of the legs, or a cold, sore lower back and knees; those lower-body and urinary signs locate the failure in the Kidney, with water overflowing upward to the Heart and Lung. A learner who starts from the palpitations would choose this.
distractorExplanations.B: Wind-Water invading the Lung is acute, with edema beginning in the face and eyelids, aversion to wind or cold and a floating pulse; this edema is chronic, starts in the legs and has a deep pulse.
distractorExplanations.D: Spleen Qi deficiency may cause mild edema with fatigue and loose stools, but it lacks the cold back and knees, the slow pulse and the palpitations from water insulting the Heart.

learningObjective: Differentiate Kidney Yang deficiency with water overflowing from simple Kidney Yang deficiency using urine volume and edema.

distinction.key: Scanty urine, pitting edema of the legs and a cold sore lower back place the failure in the Kidney; palpitations and watery sputum on lying flat are water overflowing to the Heart and Lung, not primary Heart Yang deficiency.

stem: A 49-year-old woman reports a dull, slightly burning epigastric discomfort for a year. She feels slightly hungry but has no desire to eat, feels full after small meals, and passes dry stools. Her mouth and throat are dry, especially in the afternoon, and she is thirsty but drinks only in small sips. The tongue is of normal color with a peeled patch in the center. The pulse is floating-empty at the right middle (Guan) position. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.D: Retention of Food in the Stomach

explanation: Stomach Yin deficiency deprives the Stomach of the fluids it needs to rot and ripen food, so there is hunger without desire to eat, fullness after small meals and a dull, slightly burning discomfort. Lack of fluids produces dry stools and a dry mouth and throat that worsen in the afternoon, and the thirst is for small sips because there is no Full Heat. A peeled center (the Stomach area of the tongue) and a floating-empty pulse at the right middle position confirm Stomach Yin deficiency. The discriminating findings are the peeled center and sipping thirst, as opposed to an intense thirst for cold drinks with a thick yellow coating.

distractorExplanations.A: Stomach Fire gives intense burning pain, excessive hunger, strong thirst for cold drinks, bleeding gums, a red tongue with a thick dry yellow coating and a full-rapid pulse; the learner who reads 'burning' as Full Heat overlooks the mild discomfort and peeled coating.
distractorExplanations.C: Stomach Qi deficiency causes epigastric discomfort with tiredness, a pale tongue and a weak pulse, but without dryness signs or a peeled center.
distractorExplanations.D: Retention of Food is acute and Full, with sour regurgitation, foul belching, a thick coating and a slippery-full pulse; this course is chronic and the coating is peeled.

learningObjective: Differentiate Stomach Yin deficiency from Stomach Fire by the quality of thirst, the tongue coating and the pulse.

distinction.key: Thirst for small sips with a peeled tongue center and a floating-empty right middle pulse marks Stomach Yin deficiency; intense thirst for cold drinks with a thick dry yellow coating and a full-rapid pulse marks Stomach Fire.

stem: A 30-year-old man reports sudden, severe epigastric pain that began three hours after he had several iced drinks and a bowl of ice cream on a hot day. He has vomited clear, watery fluid, feels chilly, wants only warm drinks, and finds that a hot-water bottle eases the pain. He has no sour regurgitation or foul belching. The tongue has a thick white coating. The pulse is deep, slow and tight. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.B: Retention of Food in the Stomach

explanation: Cold taken in directly through iced food and drink invades the Stomach, contracts and obstructs its Qi, and causes sudden, severe pain. Cold impairs the Stomach's descending function, so clear fluid is vomited, and the patient feels chilly, prefers warm drinks and finds the pain relieved by warmth. A thick white coating and a deep, slow, tight pulse confirm interior Full Cold. The discriminating findings are the sudden onset after cold intake and the tight pulse, which distinguish Full Cold from Empty Cold.

distractorExplanations.A: Stomach Qi deficiency is chronic, with mild discomfort, tiredness, a pale tongue and a weak pulse; it does not produce sudden, severe pain with a tight pulse.
distractorExplanations.B: Retention of Food follows overeating and shows sour regurgitation, foul belching, a thick greasy coating and a slippery pulse; these are absent.
distractorExplanations.C: Stomach deficient and Cold (Empty Cold) also prefers warmth, but it is chronic, with dull pain that improves after eating, tiredness, a pale tongue and a deep, weak pulse; the learner who sees only 'cold and prefers warmth' misses the acute onset and tight pulse of Full Cold.

stem: A 42-year-old woman reports epigastric fullness and pain for two days, beginning the night after a large holiday banquet. She has sour regurgitation, foul belching, nausea and a poor appetite, and the pain eases after she vomits. She has slept poorly, and her stools are loose and foul-smelling. The tongue has a thick, greasy coating. The pulse is full and slippery. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.A: Retention of Food in the Stomach

explanation: Overeating overwhelms the Stomach's capacity to rot and ripen, so undigested food accumulates and obstructs the descent of Stomach Qi. The stagnant food produces fullness and pain, sour regurgitation, foul belching, nausea and vomiting that relieves the pain because it removes the obstruction; it also disturbs sleep and produces loose, foul stools. A thick, greasy coating and a full, slippery pulse confirm a Full condition. The discriminating finding is the clear dietary trigger with relief from vomiting.

distractorExplanations.B: Stomach Fire shows burning pain, intense thirst, excessive hunger, bleeding gums and a red tongue with a dry yellow coating; this patient has a poor appetite and a greasy coating.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Qi invading the Stomach also causes belching and sour regurgitation, but it is triggered by emotional stress and has hypochondriac distension and a wiry pulse; the learner who links sour regurgitation only with the Liver misses the banquet trigger and the slippery pulse.
distractorExplanations.D: Stomach Qi deficiency is chronic, with mild discomfort, tiredness and a weak pulse; this presentation is acute and Full.

learningObjective: Identify Retention of Food in the Stomach from acute epigastric fullness after overeating with relief from vomiting.

distinction.key: Sour regurgitation after overeating with relief from vomiting, a thick greasy coating and a slippery pulse marks Retention of Food; emotional triggering with hypochondriac distension and a wiry pulse marks Liver Qi invading the Stomach.
