stem: A 34-year-old man reports diarrhea with mucus and blood for five days. He has abdominal pain that is not relieved by the bowel movement, urgency, foul-smelling stools and a burning sensation in the anus. He also has a low fever, a feeling of heaviness and scanty dark urine. The tongue is red with a sticky yellow coating. The pulse is slippery and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Damp-Heat lodged in the Large Intestine obstructs its function of conducting the stools and injures the vessels of the bowel, producing diarrhea with mucus (Dampness) and blood (Heat), urgency, foul stools and anal burning. Because the obstruction remains in the bowel, the pain is not relieved by defecation. Fever, heaviness and scanty dark urine show Damp-Heat, and the red tongue with a sticky yellow coating and the slippery, rapid pulse confirm it. The discriminating findings are mucus and blood in the stools with anal burning, which localize the Damp-Heat to the Large Intestine.

distractorExplanations.A: Damp-Heat in the Spleen centers on epigastric and abdominal fullness, nausea, poor appetite and loose offensive stools, sometimes with jaundice; it does not typically produce blood and mucus with anal burning. The learner who sees Damp-Heat with loose stools may stop at the Spleen.
distractorExplanations.B: Cold-Damp invading the Spleen produces loose watery stools without odor or burning, absence of thirst, a sticky white coating and a slow pulse.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Qi invading the Spleen causes stress-triggered abdominal pain relieved after the bowel movement with alternating stools and a wiry pulse; there is no fever, blood or burning.

learningObjective: Differentiate Large Intestine Damp-Heat from Damp-Heat in the Spleen in acute diarrhea.

distinction.key: Mucus and blood in the stools with anal burning and pain unrelieved by defecation mark Large Intestine Damp-Heat; epigastric fullness, nausea and poor appetite mark Damp-Heat in the Spleen.

stem: A 29-year-old woman reports burning, painful urination with urgency and frequency for three days. Her urine is dark yellow and cloudy. She has a slight fever, a feeling of heaviness in the lower abdomen, and thirst without a desire to drink. She has no mouth ulcers or mental restlessness. The tongue has a thick, sticky yellow coating on the root. The pulse is slippery and rapid, especially at the left rear (Chi) position. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?

options.A: Kidney Yin deficiency with Empty Fire
options.C: Full Heat in the Small Intestine

explanation: Damp-Heat in the Bladder obstructs its Qi transformation, causing burning, painful, urgent and frequent urination with dark, cloudy urine; the cloudiness reflects Dampness. Fever and thirst without a desire to drink show Heat combined with Dampness, and heaviness in the lower abdomen reflects Dampness in the Lower Burner. The thick, sticky yellow coating on the root and the slippery, rapid pulse at the left rear position confirm Damp-Heat in the Bladder. The discriminating finding is cloudy urine with a sticky yellow root coating.

distractorExplanations.A: Kidney Yin deficiency with Empty Fire can produce scanty dark urine, but without burning and urgency, and with night sweats, a coatless red tongue and a floating-empty pulse; this presentation is acute and Full.
distractorExplanations.C: Full Heat in the Small Intestine derives from Heart Fire and shows mouth and tongue ulcers, mental restlessness and a red, swollen tip with an overflowing pulse at the left front; these are absent, and the sticky coating indicates Dampness.
distractorExplanations.D: Kidney Qi not firm causes frequent pale urine with dribbling, a pale tongue and a weak pulse; burning and cloudy dark urine indicate Damp-Heat.

learningObjective: Explain how Damp-Heat in the Bladder produces burning, cloudy, urgent urination.

distinction.key: Cloudy urine with a sticky yellow coating on the tongue root marks Bladder Damp-Heat; mouth ulcers, restlessness and a red tongue tip mark Full Heat in the Small Intestine.

stem: Timidity, lack of courage and initiative, indecisiveness, being easily startled and frequent sighing, accompanied by a pale tongue and a weak pulse, are most characteristic of which pattern?
explanation: In Zang Fu theory the Gallbladder controls decisiveness and gives a person courage and initiative. When Gallbladder Qi is deficient, the person is timid, lacks initiative, cannot make decisions and is easily startled; sighing is also described. The pale tongue and weak pulse show a deficient rather than Full condition. The discriminating features are the mental-emotional signs of indecision and lack of courage with deficiency findings.

distractorExplanations.A: Gallbladder Damp-Heat is a Full pattern with hypochondriac pain, a bitter taste, nausea, possible jaundice, a sticky yellow coating and a slippery-wiry pulse; it does not center on timidity.
distractorExplanations.B: Liver Qi stagnation also features sighing, but with distension, irritability, mood swings and a wiry pulse; a weak pulse and pale tongue rule it out. The learner who links sighing only to Liver Qi stagnation would choose it.
distractorExplanations.C: Kidney Yang deficiency is linked to fear through Five Element correspondence, but the pattern is defined by Cold, backache, abundant clear urine and a deep, slow pulse, none of which is given; a learner equating timidity with fear would pick it.

learningObjective: Identify the mental-emotional signs that characterize Gallbladder deficiency.

distinction.key: Timidity and indecision with a weak pulse mark Gallbladder deficiency; sighing with distension, irritability and a wiry pulse marks Liver Qi stagnation.

stem: An 81-year-old woman reports constipation for two years, passing small, dry, pellet-like stools every three to four days with great difficulty. Her mouth, throat and skin are dry, she is thin, and she has occasional dizziness. She has no abdominal distension, anal burning or thirst for cold drinks. The tongue is pale and dry. The pulse is thin (thready). Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: In the elderly, declining Blood and fluids leave the Large Intestine without moisture, so stools become dry, small and difficult to pass. A dry mouth, throat and skin, a thin body and dizziness reflect a general insufficiency of fluids and Blood. A pale, dry tongue and a thin pulse confirm a deficiency of fluids without Heat. The discriminating finding is dry stools with dryness elsewhere and no Heat signs.

distractorExplanations.B: Heat in the Large Intestine also dries the stools, but with anal burning, thirst for cold drinks, a red tongue with a dry yellow coating and a full-rapid pulse; the learner who equates dry stools with Heat misses the pale tongue and thin pulse.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Qi stagnation causes constipation with small, bitty stools, abdominal distension, irritability and a wiry pulse; there is no distension and the pulse is thin.
distractorExplanations.D: Spleen Qi deficiency causes difficult bowel movements with stools that are not dry, fatigue after defecation, a pale swollen tongue and a weak pulse; the dryness signs point to a lack of fluids.

learningObjective: Differentiate Large Intestine Dryness from Heat in the Large Intestine in chronic constipation.

distinction.key: Dry stools with a pale dry tongue and a thin pulse mark Large Intestine Dryness; dry stools with anal burning, thirst, a yellow coating and a full-rapid pulse mark Heat in the Large Intestine.

stem: A 37-year-old woman reports abdominal pain with loose stools for eighteen months. Episodes flare when she is stressed or angry, the pain eases after the bowel movement, and her stools alternate between loose and constipated. She also has abdominal distension, flatulence, irritability, tiredness and a poor appetite. The tongue is slightly red on the sides with a thin white coating. The pulse is wiry on the left and weak on the right. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Stagnant Liver Qi overacts on the Spleen along the controlling (Ke) cycle and disrupts its transformation and transportation. The Liver side shows as stress-triggered episodes, distension, flatulence, irritability, red tongue sides and a wiry left pulse; the Spleen side shows as tiredness, poor appetite, loose stools and a weak right pulse. Pain that eases after the bowel movement and stools that alternate between loose and constipated are typical of this disharmony. The discriminating finding is the split pulse, wiry on the left and weak on the right, showing that both organs are involved.

distractorExplanations.A: Liver Qi stagnation alone explains the distension and emotional triggering but not the tiredness, poor appetite and weak right pulse; the learner who sees only the stress trigger stops here.
distractorExplanations.B: Spleen Qi deficiency alone explains the tiredness and loose stools but not the emotional triggering, red tongue sides or wiry left pulse.
distractorExplanations.D: Large Intestine Damp-Heat is acute, with mucus and blood in the stools, anal burning, a sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse; none of these is present.

learningObjective: Analyze a combined Liver-Spleen disharmony using the split left-right pulse and the emotional trigger.

distinction.key: Emotional triggering, red tongue sides and a wiry left pulse added to Spleen deficiency signs mark Liver Qi invading the Spleen rather than Spleen Qi deficiency alone.

stem: A 52-year-old woman reports insomnia for one year, with difficulty falling asleep and frequent waking. She has palpitations, mental restlessness, poor memory, dizziness, tinnitus, a sore lower back, night sweats, heat in the palms and soles, and scanty dark urine. The tongue is red with no coating and a redder tip. The pulse is rapid, weak at both rear (Chi) positions and relatively overflowing at both front (Cun) positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Kidney Yin fails to rise to nourish the Heart, and Heart Fire fails to descend to warm the Kidney, so Water and Fire lose their communication. Kidney Yin deficiency gives dizziness, tinnitus, a sore lower back, night sweats, five-palm heat and scanty dark urine; Empty Heat in the Heart gives insomnia, palpitations, mental restlessness and poor memory. The red, coatless tongue with a redder tip and a pulse weak at the rear but relatively overflowing at the front show deficiency below with Heat above. The discriminating findings are the Heart signs (palpitations, insomnia, redder tip, front pulses) joined to Kidney Yin deficiency.

distractorExplanations.A: Kidney Yin deficiency alone explains the back pain, tinnitus and night sweats but not the palpitations, insomnia, redder tongue tip and overflowing front pulses; the learner who stops at the root misses the Heart.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver and Kidney Yin deficiency adds dry eyes, blurred vision, numbness of the limbs and scanty menstruation, showing Liver rather than Heart involvement.
distractorExplanations.D: Heart and Spleen deficiency (Heart Blood with Spleen Qi deficiency) also causes insomnia, palpitations and poor memory, but with a pale tongue, poor appetite, fatigue and a thin-weak pulse, and no Heat signs.

learningObjective: Analyze the combined pattern of Heart and Kidney not harmonized by linking Heart Empty Heat signs to Kidney Yin deficiency.

distinction.key: Palpitations, insomnia, a redder tongue tip and relatively overflowing front pulses added to Kidney Yin signs mark Heart and Kidney not harmonized.

stem: A 66-year-old man reports loose stools for two years, with urgent diarrhea just before dawn that contains undigested food. He has a poor appetite, abdominal distension after meals that is worse after cold food, and tiredness. His abdomen and lower back feel cold and his limbs are cold. He passes abundant clear urine and his ankles are slightly puffy. The tongue is pale, swollen, wet and teeth-marked. The pulse is deep, weak and slow. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Kidney Yang is the root of Spleen Yang; when both fail, food is not transformed (undigested food in the stools, poor appetite, tiredness) and the Lower Burner is cold. Diarrhea just before dawn, the classic 'cock's crow' diarrhea, occurs at the hour when Yang should be rising but the Kidney fire is too weak. A cold abdomen, back and limbs, abundant clear urine, slight edema, a pale, swollen, wet, teeth-marked tongue and a deep, weak, slow pulse confirm combined Yang deficiency. The discriminating finding is the coexistence of Spleen signs (undigested food, poor appetite, teeth marks) with Kidney signs (dawn diarrhea, cold back, clear urine).

distractorExplanations.A: Spleen Qi deficiency causes tiredness and loose stools but without marked Cold, dawn diarrhea, a cold back or a slow pulse; the learner who reads loose stools as a Spleen problem alone misses the Yang and Kidney signs.
distractorExplanations.B: Spleen Yang deficiency explains the loose stools, undigested food, cold abdomen, poor appetite and teeth-marked tongue, but not diarrhea specifically before dawn, a cold lower back, abundant clear urine and puffy ankles; those are Kidney Yang signs, so both Yang are deficient. A learner who stops at the digestive picture would choose this.
distractorExplanations.C: Cold-Damp invading the Spleen is usually acute, with heaviness, a thick sticky white coating and a slippery pulse, rather than a two-year course with a deep, weak pulse and Kidney signs.

learningObjective: Analyze chronic dawn diarrhea as a combined Spleen and Kidney Yang deficiency.

distinction.key: Dawn diarrhea, a cold lower back, abundant clear urine and puffy ankles add the Kidney to a Spleen Yang picture; without them the pattern is Spleen Yang deficiency alone.

stem: A 58-year-old woman reports dry, gritty eyes and blurred vision for two years. She also has dizziness, a low-pitched tinnitus, a sore and weak lower back and knees, numbness of the limbs, night sweats and a dry throat at night. She has no headache, irritability or palpitations. The tongue is red with no coating. The pulse is thin (thready) and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: The Liver and Kidney share a common source, Liver Blood and Kidney Essence nourishing each other, so Yin deficiency of one readily involves the other. Liver Yin deficiency fails to moisten the eyes and nourish the sinews, giving dry, gritty eyes, blurred vision and numbness; Kidney Yin deficiency gives a low-pitched tinnitus, dizziness and a sore, weak back and knees. Night sweats, a dry throat at night, a red coatless tongue and a thin, rapid pulse show Yin deficiency with Empty Heat. The discriminating findings are the eye symptoms (Liver) and the back and ear symptoms (Kidney) together with Yin-deficiency Heat signs.

distractorExplanations.B: Liver Blood deficiency also causes blurred vision, dizziness and numbness, but with a pale tongue, a pale complexion and no night sweats or Heat; the red coatless tongue and Kidney signs rule it out.
distractorExplanations.C: Heart and Kidney not harmonized presents Kidney Yin signs with palpitations, insomnia and a redder tongue tip; this patient has no Heart signs.
distractorExplanations.D: Liver Yang rising, which can develop from this pattern, adds headache, irritability, a red face and a wiry pulse; none of these is present.

learningObjective: Analyze Liver and Kidney Yin deficiency by assigning eye, ear and lower back findings to their organs.

distinction.key: Eye and limb symptoms with night sweats, Kidney signs and a red coatless tongue mark Liver and Kidney Yin deficiency; the same eye symptoms with a pale tongue and no Heat mark Liver Blood deficiency.

stem: A 61-year-old man reports a dry cough with occasional blood-streaked sputum for one year. He is breathless on exertion and has a hoarse voice, a dry throat at night, a sore lower back, night sweats, an afternoon malar flush and a thin body. The tongue is red and peeled. The pulse is thin (thready) and rapid, weakest at the right front (Cun) and both rear (Chi) positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Kidney Yin is the root of the Yin of all organs, and the Lung and Kidney are linked through the generating (Sheng) cycle, Metal generating Water, and through respiration. Lung Yin deficiency produces the dry cough, blood-streaked sputum, hoarse voice and dry throat; Kidney Yin deficiency adds the sore lower back and weakens the Kidney's grasp of Qi, contributing to breathlessness on exertion. Night sweats, an afternoon malar flush, a red peeled tongue and a thin, rapid pulse show Empty Heat. The discriminating finding is Kidney involvement (sore back, weak rear pulses) added to Lung Yin deficiency.

distractorExplanations.A: Lung Yin deficiency alone explains the dry cough and Empty Heat but not the sore lower back and weak rear pulses; the learner who stops at the chief complaint misses the Kidney.
distractorExplanations.B: Kidney failing to receive Qi is a Qi or Yang deficiency with difficult inhalation, cold limbs, a pale tongue and a deep, weak pulse; here the tongue is red and peeled and there are Heat signs.
distractorExplanations.D: Dryness injuring the Lung is a recent exterior condition with a thin dry coating and no night sweats or back pain; this course is chronic and the coating is peeled.

learningObjective: Analyze Lung and Kidney Yin deficiency by identifying Kidney signs alongside a chronic Yin-deficient cough.

distinction.key: A sore lower back and weak rear pulses added to a dry cough with Empty Heat mark Lung and Kidney Yin deficiency rather than Lung Yin deficiency alone.

stem: A 45-year-old man reports fits of coughing for three weeks that are set off by arguments or frustration. He coughs up scanty, sticky yellow sputum, occasionally streaked with blood, and has pain in the chest and hypochondrium. He is irritable, with a red face, red eyes, a bitter taste and thirst. The tongue is red with redder sides and a dry yellow coating. The pulse is wiry and rapid. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: Liver Fire rises and insults the Lung, Wood rebelling against Metal in the reverse direction of the controlling cycle. Rising Fire obstructs the descent of Lung Qi and scorches fluids, causing paroxysmal coughing with scanty, sticky yellow and sometimes blood-streaked sputum. Emotional triggering, hypochondriac and chest pain, irritability, a red face and eyes, a bitter taste, redder tongue sides and a wiry, rapid pulse show that the Fire originates in the Liver. The discriminating findings are the anger-triggered cough with Liver signs and a wiry rather than slippery pulse.

distractorExplanations.A: Phlegm-Heat in the Lung produces profuse, thick yellow sputum, chest oppression, a thick sticky yellow coating and a slippery-rapid pulse; scanty sputum, red sides and a wiry pulse point to the Liver. The learner who sees yellow sputum and stops at the Lung would choose it.
distractorExplanations.C: Liver Fire blazing explains the red face, red eyes, bitter taste and irritability but does not account for the cough; when Liver Fire specifically disturbs the Lung, the combined diagnosis is more precise.
distractorExplanations.D: Wind-Heat is an acute exterior pattern with fever, aversion to cold, a sore throat and a floating-rapid pulse; there are no exterior signs.

learningObjective: Analyze a cough caused by Liver Fire insulting the Lung by recognizing Liver signs and the emotional trigger.

distinction.key: An anger-triggered cough with scanty sputum, redder tongue sides and a wiry-rapid pulse marks Liver Fire insulting the Lung; profuse yellow sputum with a thick sticky coating and a slippery pulse marks Phlegm-Heat.

stem: A 12-year-old boy is brought in for a cough with thin, white, watery sputum that has persisted for two years and flares every winter. He is short of breath on exertion, has a weak voice, sweats easily and catches colds often. He also has a poor appetite, abdominal distension after eating, loose stools and tiredness. The tongue is pale and teeth-marked with a thin white coating. The pulse is weak, especially at the right front (Cun) and middle (Guan) positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate pattern diagnosis?
explanation: The Spleen (Earth) generates the Lung (Metal), and the Gu Qi produced by the Spleen is the basis of Lung Qi and Wei Qi. When both are deficient, Lung signs (a weak cough with thin, watery sputum, breathlessness on exertion, a weak voice, spontaneous sweating, frequent colds) coexist with Spleen signs (poor appetite, distension after eating, loose stools, tiredness). The pale, teeth-marked tongue and a weak pulse at the right front (Lung) and right middle (Spleen) positions confirm involvement of both organs. The discriminating finding is the combination of respiratory and digestive deficiency signs with weakness at both right-side positions.

distractorExplanations.A: Lung Qi deficiency alone explains the cough, weak voice and sweating but not the poor appetite, loose stools, teeth marks and weak right middle pulse.
distractorExplanations.B: Spleen Qi deficiency alone explains the digestive signs and tiredness but not the chronic cough, spontaneous sweating and frequent colds.
distractorExplanations.C: Phlegm-Damp obstructing the Lung produces profuse sticky sputum, chest oppression, a thick sticky coating and a slippery pulse; here the sputum is thin and watery and the coating thin.

learningObjective: Analyze a combined Lung and Spleen Qi deficiency by linking respiratory and digestive signs through the generating cycle.

distinction.key: Poor appetite, loose stools, teeth marks and a weak right middle pulse added to a weak cough with sweating mark Lung and Spleen Qi deficiency rather than Lung Qi deficiency alone.
